title: LL.B. - Bachelor of Laws Programme
description: Students are required to complete a minimum of 90 units of courses as follows:

sections.title: Elective Courses
text: Any LAWS elective courses at 1000 – 4000 level (of which 21 units are currently prescribed as prerequisites for admission into the Postgraduate Certificate in Laws (PCLL) Programme)

subsections.title: Streams
text: Students may choose to declare the Chinese Law Stream and/or the Global Law Stream within the LLB Programme by taking the following courses:

notes.text: All LAWS courses, excluding courses labelled as r and LAWS2220, will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

Students can opt to use LAWS2201 “Chinese Law (Summer Course)” successfully completed at the Tsinghua University to fulfill 3 units out of the 5-unit University Core Chinese Language Requirement in which case LAWS2201 will not be counted towards the fulfillment of elective courses requirement.

Exemption from 7 units out of the 8-unit University Core English Language Requirement bases on the equivalence of courses to be taken by students (LAWS1010, 1020, 1041, 1042, 1100, 2110, 2121, 2131, 4151). Students are required to take a 1-unit ELTU course to fulfill the requirement.
In addition to Major Programme Requirement and University Core Requirement, students are required to take 12 units of non-law electives.

Students who opt for the Study Option offered by King’s College London (KCL) and have successfully completed the Optional Modules of 120 credits offered by KCL’s Master of Laws (LLM) Programme will be granted course and unit exemption for up to 18 units of Major Elective Courses.

Students who opt for the Study Option offered by the University of Southern California USC Gould School of Law (USC) and have successfully completed 21 units of USC LLM courses will be granted course and unit exemption for up to 18 units of Major Elective Courses.
Students who opt for the Study Option offered by KCL will be required to take LAWS4001 to substitute for LAWS4010 in order to fulfill the capstone requirement.

Prerequisites for subsequent admission into the PCLL Programme. A full list of PCLL prerequisites is listed below:LAWS1020, 1041, 1042, 1100, 2101, 2102, 2110, 2121, 2122, 2131, 2132, 3130, 3151, 3152, 4002, 4120, 4151, 4152

parts.title: 2nd Degree: Bachelor of Arts (Translation)
parts.description: Students are required to complete a minimum of 57 units of courses as follows:

sections.title: Elective Courses
text: Students are required to complete 39 units of elective courses from the following lists of courses, including at least one course from each of Electives Cluster A and Electives Cluster B:

notes.text: TRAN courses at 2000 and above level will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

Translation Major students are expected to be proficient in both English and Chinese. Students may therefore wish to consider taking courses that emphasize writing and speaking skills as part of their free electives, on top of the major programme requirement. Listed below are courses for reference: Course for writing skills in Chinese CHLL3403 Creative Writing Course for oral expression skills in Cantonese CHLT1302 Oral Communication Skills Courses for oral expression skills in Putonghua CLCP3703 Advanced Putonghua CLCP4713 Current Affairs and Discussion CLCP4723 Academic Presentation and Discussion Courses for writing skills in English ENGE3260 Creative Writing ELTU3413 Research Writing in the Humanities and Social Sciences Courses for oral expression skills in English ENGE2100 Research and Oral Reporting ELTU3502 Essentials of Public Speaking

For those students who have chosen TRAN4900 Translation Thesis, the language used in writing the thesis should be different from the target language of their translation project for TRAN4510/4520 (e.g. if the student writes the TRAN4900 thesis in English, s/he must take TRAN4510 Translation Project: English-Chinese for Final Year Project).

parts.title: 2nd Degree: Bachelor of Social Science (Sociology)
parts.description: Students are required to complete a minimum of 60 units of courses as follows:

notes.text: SOCI courses at 2000 and above level will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.
Sociology Field Studies (SOCI3245)
rows: The field studies should have a strong component matching the theme of a particular concentration in order to fulfill the requirement of that concentration area.

If a student declares to take two concentration areas, units earned from the course “Sociology Field Studies” will be counted towards the fulfillment of the requirement of one area only, subject to the course supervisor’s endorsement. The student should indicate towards which area the units are counted when declaring the concentrations.

If a student has taken SOCI3245 and 4211, only up to 3 units from either one course can be counted towards the fulfillment of the concentration requirement, also subject to the course supervisor’s endorsement.

notes.text: Sociology Internship: Nurturing Competency for Meeting Future Challenges (SOCI4211)
rows: The internship organisation and/or the internship job nature should have a strong component matching the theme of a particular concentration in order to fulfill the requirement of that concentration area, subject to the course supervisor’s endorsement.

If a student declares to take two concentration areas, units earned from the course “Sociology Internship: Nurturing Competency for Meeting Future Challenges” will be counted towards the fulfillment of the requirement of one area only, subject to the course supervisor’s endorsement. The student should indicate towards which area the units are counted when declaring the concentrations.

If a student has taken SOCI3245 and 4211, only up to 3 units from either one course can be counted towards the fulfillment of the concentration requirement, also subject to the course supervisor’s endorsement.

notes.text: Graduation Thesis II (SOCI4020)
rows: The Graduation Thesis should have a strong component matching the theme of a particular concentration in order to fulfill the requirement of that concentration area.

If a student declares to take two concentration areas, units earned from the course “Graduation Thesis II” will be counted towards the fulfillment of the requirement of one area only, subject to the course supervisor’s endorsement. The student should indicate towards which area the units are counted when declaring the concentrations.

notes.text: Directed Studies I/II (SOCI4410/4420)
rows: The Directed Studies should have a strong component matching the theme of a particular concentration in order to fulfill the requirement of that concentration area.

If a student has taken SOCI4410 and 4420, and both are of the same theme that can be counted towards the fulfillment of the requirement of one concentration only, then only up to 3 units from either one course can be counted towards the fulfillment of the concentration requirement, also subject to the course supervisor’s endorsement.

If a student has taken SOCI4410 and 4420 with different themes, subject to the course supervisor’s endorsement, the units earned from SOCI4410 can be counted towards the fulfillment of the requirement of one concentration and SOCI4420 towards another.
Units earned from a directed studies course can only be counted towards the fulfillment of the requirement of one concentration.

notes.text: Students are required to take either SOCI3227 or 3236 in order to fulfill the requirement of Required Courses. If a student has taken both SOCI3227 and 3236, the extra 3 units earned can be counted towards the fulfillment of the requirement of Elective Courses.

Students are required to take either SOCI3002 or 3241 or 4204 in order to fulfill the requirement of Required Courses. If a student has taken more than one of these three courses, the extra 3 units or 6 units earned can be counted towards the fulfillment of the requirement of Elective Courses.

supplementary_note_sections.title: Explanatory Notes on Mutual Recognition or Exclusion

notes.text: The 12-unit non-law electives can be used to satisfy the requirements of both the first and second degrees.
